title: Design System: Agentic Data Intelligence Platform

ui.purpose: Every control, label, table cell and heading in the app chrome.

narrative.purpose: A report's prose only - larger, looser, measured to ~72ch so it reads as a document rather than another panel.

data.purpose: Anything a reader copies, compares digit-by-digit, or verifies: ids, timestamps, scores, counts, code.

ramp.note: Named utilities defined in frontend/src/index.css's @theme block. The token is the only way to express a step; literals repeated at call sites are a second representation of the same fact.

shadows.name: toast-ambient
shadows.purpose: The ONLY shadow in the system. Reserved for the toast, which genuinely floats above the page. Ordinary content is flat by default.

shadows.name: aurora-glow
shadows.purpose: Aurora only. Applied to exactly two things - the primary action and the current nav item - so a demo audience finds both instantly. A STATIC box-shadow: nothing in this system pulses or animates at rest.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Color-only transitions on hover/active. Nothing animates position, size, or opacity at rest - no ambient motion implying activity that isn't happening.

effects.name: aurora-panel-filter
effects.purpose: Frosted glass, applied only via the .panel class. Resolves to none on the operate themes.

effects.name: aurora-page-backdrop
effects.purpose: Aurora's gradient ground. The washes were dimmed from their first values because the brighter top-left lobe sat behind the sidebar glass and lowered worst-case text contrast.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one affirmative action on a surface - Load, Register, Ask, Predict, Approve.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: var(--color-brand-600, #0B6E6E); color: #fff; border: none; border-radius: 4px; padding: 6px 14px; font: 500 13px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-brand-700, #095A5A); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-brand-600, #0B6E6E); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.6; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Reserved for the single irreversible action, 'Discard run (permanent)'. Never used for an ordinary reject or dismiss - its colour is what tells a reader this one cannot be undone, before they read the label.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #fff; color: #B91C1C; border: 1px solid #B91C1C; border-radius: 4px; padding: 6px 14px; font: 500 13px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #FBEBEB; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #B91C1C; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: A verdict, readable at a glance. A filled dot carries the state by shape and colour before the word is read - the label is always present too, so status never depends on colour alone.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 2px 10px; font: 500 12px system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-badge-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: currentColor; } .ds-badge-positive { background: #E8F5EC; color: #15803D; }

components.name: Card / Panel
components.description: The default container. Flat, 1px-bordered, 6px radius, no shadow - depth comes from tone and stroke, never a floating illusion. Cards never nest.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #E2E5EA; border-radius: 6px; padding: 20px; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0 0 4px; font: 600 15px system-ui, sans-serif; color: #12161C; } .ds-card-sub { margin: 0; font: 400 13px system-ui, sans-serif; color: #4B5563; }

components.name: Quality Context Panel
components.description: The most important panel in the product. Renders FIRST on a report, above the narrative, in a full-perimeter caution border with a tinted fill - structurally a different card, not a decorated one. A fluent report reading as authoritative over repaired or unvalidated data is the single most harmful thing this UI can render, so this treatment is a hard product constraint, not a style choice.
components.html:
Data quality context

The active baseline for this source is still PROVISIONAL.
components.css: .ds-quality { border: 1px solid #9A6700; background: #FBF2DE; border-radius: 6px; padding: 24px; } .ds-quality-title { margin: 0 0 8px; font: 600 15px system-ui, sans-serif; color: #9A6700; } .ds-quality-body { max-width: 68ch; font: 400 13px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; color: #12161C; white-space: pre-wrap; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Form controls read as controls: a stroke and a small radius, never a filled pill.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" placeholder="run number (e.g. 17) or full run id" />
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: #fff; border: 1px solid #C7CCD4; border-radius: 4px; padding: 6px 12px; font: 400 13px system-ui, sans-serif; color: #12161C; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #6B7280; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-brand-600, #0B6E6E); outline-offset: 1px; border-color: var(--color-brand-600, #0B6E6E); }

components.name: Sidebar Navigation
components.description: Fixed graphite rail. Active state is carried by text/icon colour plus a background lift - no accent bar, because a decorative colour bar is refused everywhere else in this system and the nav gets no exception.
components.html: ReportsAudit
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; background: #141922; padding: 12px; width: 220px; } .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px 12px; color: #B8C0CC; font: 500 13px system-ui, sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.05); color: #fff; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); color: #fff; }

components.name: Data Table
components.description: Sunken header row, 1px row dividers, no zebra striping. Numerics right-aligned and tabular; ids monospaced and de-emphasised. Always inside its own horizontal-scroll container so the page body never scrolls sideways.
components.css: .ds-table-wrap { overflow-x: auto; } .ds-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font: 400 13px system-ui, sans-serif; color: #12161C; } .ds-table th { background: #F1F3F6; color: #4B5563; font-weight: 500; text-align: left; padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #E2E5EA; } .ds-table td { padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #E2E5EA; } .ds-table .ds-num { text-align: right; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-table .ds-id { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 12px; color: #6B7280; }

narrative.overview:
This is a diagnostic instrument, not a product pitch. The system ingests data, decides what it can safely fix and what it can't, and shows a human exactly why - the interface's job is to make that reasoning legible at a glance, the same way a calibrated lab instrument or an avionics status panel reads: quiet at rest, unambiguous the moment something needs attention, never decorative for its own sake.

The prior implementation used a violet/purple accent (#7c5cff) inherited from an unmodified Tailwind starter palette, rounded-2xl cards with soft shadows stacked in undifferentiated columns, and no typographic distinction between a report's prose and its surrounding chrome. All three read as generic AI-dashboard default rather than a considered instrument, and are retired by this system.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, bordered surfaces - no drop shadows on ordinary content, depth comes from tone and a 1px border, never a floating card illusion.
One accent color (a deep signal teal) used sparingly for actions and active state; everything else is ink, paper, and border grays.
Status is color- and shape-coded (a filled dot plus a muted pill), never plain text a reader has to parse.
Data (ids, timestamps, scores, counts) is monospaced and visually quieter than the judgment it supports; prose (a report's narrative) is set larger and looser than the UI chrome around it.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal teal appears on primary actions, the active nav item, links, and focus rings only - never as a decorative fill, never as a background wash. If a screen has more than a few teal elements, something has drifted into decoration.

rules.name: The Status-Never-Accent Rule
rules.body: The four status colors and the one accent color are never the same hue family. A reader must be able to tell 'this is the brand color' from 'this is a verdict' without reading the label.

rules.name: The Reading vs. Scanning Rule
rules.body: A report's narrative and recommendations are set at reading scale with a measured width and no card chrome, so they read as a document. Charts, evidence and tables stay at UI/data scale inside bordered panels, so they read as instruments. The two are never the same weight.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. The only shadow in the system belongs to the toast, which genuinely floats above the page.

rules.name: The Skin-Not-Surgery Rule
rules.body: A theme may change how a surface looks. It may never change what it says, what it emphasises, or what it lets a human do. Every E2E spec runs unmodified against all three themes.

rules.name: The Substantive Tint Rule
rules.body: A status tint is a SURFACE, not a wash. On a gradient ground a low-alpha tint let the violet through and a status panel read as decoration - which is precisely what the Quality Context panel must never do.

rules.name: The Measured-Not-Eyeballed Rule
rules.body: No theme ships on a colour judged by eye. Every text node on every page in every theme is measured by two independent methods and the worse is taken.

dos: Do render Quality Context first on every report, in the caution-tinted panel, above the narrative - never a footnote.
Do keep generation mode (llm/template) visible as a plain badge near the report title on every report, in every mode.
Do right-align every numeric table column and monospace-mute every id column.
Do show a live elapsed-time counter on every long-running action (ingest, resolve, predict) - never a bare spinner with no sense of progress.
Do list every gate reason in full on an escalated item - this is the accountability argument; it is never truncated, collapsed, or hidden behind a tooltip.
Do render a correlated group of validation failures as exactly one item with one set of decision buttons.
donts: Don't use purple, violet, or any gradient anywhere in this system.
Don't add a drop shadow to an element that isn't genuinely floating above the page.
Don't nest a card inside another card - use a sunken sub-region or a divider instead.
Don't use caused, drove, impact, because of, or any causal phrasing in UI copy, empty states, or labels - correlation is never presented as causation, in the chrome any more than in a report's prose.
Don't let 'Discard run (permanent)' read as a fourth variant of the three recoverable decisions - it keeps its own color (danger), its own visual separation, and its confirmation step.
Don't give a card a corner radius larger than 6px, or a button/badge larger than 4px.
Don't let a theme auto-select Aurora - it is opt-in, and first-visit detection resolves only to Default or Dark.
